transcript: Pulitzer winner James Ijames is back at The Public with Good Bones, a new play about gentrification and in a broader sense, ownership. As a woman named Aisha settles into her new home with her husband in the area she grew up in, she finds herself mentally suspended between the way she experienced it growing up and her circumstances now. Being an urban planner and working on initiatives that aim to revitalize the area further complicates things, especially with her contractor. This play is dense and there's a lot of explicit debate about gentrification, community, and displacement. But unlike a lot of other plays that tackle timely issues head-on, this play still grounds its conversations in a reasonably believable plot with pretty developed characters. Oh, and good acting always helps too. With that, another playbill for my collection.
